heroDescription: Tarigato runs two coding agents on a Go project. One changes the code; the other writes a test for a possible bug. The Go controller checks their work and saves the patches for your review.
demoNote: Browser simulation. No agents run and no files change.
readyText: Press play to explore the run.
codeInitial: The existing tests miss the exact expiry time.
initialDescription: The code accepts a session at its exact expiry time. The task is to reject it.
architectureNote: Two roles, one controller, and at most one repair.
exampleDescription: The code accepts a session at its exact expiry time. Change >= to > and test the boundary.
installDescription: Build the CLI, select a committed Go project, and state the task.
rulesDescription: Protected files, accepted tests, and the one-repair limit.
limitsDescription: Trusted projects, provider coverage, and what checks cannot prove.
copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the command and copy it manually.
baselineDescription: Tarigato starts from a clean, committed Go repository. At least one named test must pass before any agent runs.
builderDescription: The builder edits production Go code. Existing tests, dependencies, and configuration are protected.
candidateDescription: Tarigato reconstructs the patch in a fresh workspace and reruns the original tests. A regression stops the run.
challengerDescription: The challenger sees the candidate in a separate session. It can submit one new test file with one named test, or report no finding.
verify1Description: The controller checks that the submitted test actually ran and that the original tests still pass.
verify2Description: A second run must produce the same assertion outcome. An invalid or inconsistent result goes to human review.
repairDescription: A reproduced assertion failure allows the builder role one repair. The challenge test is frozen and cannot be changed.
finalDescription: The final source and any accepted challenge test must pass in another fresh workspace.
reportDescription: Tarigato saves patches, test observations, and a report. It does not apply changes, merge, or push.
inconclusiveDescription: The challenge passed once and failed once. Tarigato cannot admit a stable result, so it stops without a repair.
codeChanged: The equality boundary now rejects expired sessions.
codeUnfixed: The candidate still accepts a session at exact expiry.
codeTest: The challenger submits one boundary test.
codeUnstable: Illustrative test that depends on wall-clock timing.
codeArtifacts: Review source, test expectations, and the recorded checks.
branchNote: A stable failing challenge permits one repair. An invalid result stops the run.
baselineBlockText: Read the committed repository and run the existing suite. The source checkout stays unchanged.
baselineBlockNote: Requires a root go.mod, a clean checkout, and at least one passing named test.
builderBlockText: The first agent implements the task in a separate Git workspace. Only production Go files may change.
builderBlockNote: Existing tests, dependencies, configuration, testdata, vendor, and .github are protected.
candidateBlockText: Reconstruct the candidate from its patch and check that the original tests still pass.
candidateBlockNote: Builder regressions stop the run; they do not trigger the challenge-repair turn.
challengerBlockText: A separate agent session receives the candidate and tries to express a counterexample as one new named test.
challengerBlockNote: No finding is allowed. A critique alone does not count as a reproduced failure.
verifyBlockText: Run the admitted test in two fresh workspaces. Confirm its identity and keep the original tests passing.
verifyBlockNote: Missing tests, crashes, compilation errors, and inconsistent outcomes remain inconclusive.
repairBlockText: Only a stable assertion failure permits a repair. A fresh session in the builder role receives the failure evidence.
repairBlockNote: The admitted challenge test stays frozen. There is no second repair.
finalBlockText: Rebuild from the final source patch and accepted test patch, then run the checks in a fresh workspace.
finalBlockNote: The result records observed tests. It is not a proof of correctness.
reportBlockText: Read report.md, inspect changes.patch and tests.patch, and decide whether to accept the result.
reportBlockNote: No automatic apply, merge, commit, or push.
sourceBlockText: The committed source is the starting point. Tarigato does its work in separate copies.
sourceBlockNote: Ignored files are not copied into the run. Use trusted repositories.
controlBlockText: One foreground Go process owns the sequence, enforces file restrictions, runs checks, and saves evidence.
controlBlockNote: There is no judge agent, background service, database, or configuration file.
builderWorkBlockText: A disposable Git clone holds the implementation. The resulting patch is reconstructed and checked.
builderWorkBlockNote: The source repository is not the agent working directory.
challengerWorkBlockText: A fresh copy of the candidate isolates the challenger session from the builder session.
challengerWorkBlockNote: Separate workspaces are not operating-system sandboxes.
checksWorkBlockText: Candidate, challenge, and final checks use fresh copies reconstructed from patches.
checksWorkBlockNote: Checks parse Go test events and retain bounded diagnostics.
artifactsBlockText: Review artifacts are saved under ~/.tarigato/runs/<id>/. Successful runs remove their workspaces.
artifactsBlockNote: Unsuccessful runs retain any created workspaces for inspection.
docsEnglishNote: This detailed article is currently available in English. The quickstart is translated.
docsMissing: This article could not be loaded. Use the source documentation below.
scenarioHelp: The passing path follows the recorded example. Repair and unstable-test paths are illustrative.
branchStop: Invalid or unstable: stop for review
boundaryBug: At exact expiry, the candidate accepts an expired session.
boundaryFixed: The repaired expression rejects exact expiry.
boundaryAgreement: Away from the boundary, both expressions agree.
boundaryNote: The expression runs locally in JavaScript. The workflow below is simulated; agents and Go tests do not run here.
gameTheory: The two roles have opposing objectives set by their instructions. There are no scores, numerical rewards, or equilibrium calculations.
gameBuilderMove: Change production Go code. Existing tests stay protected.
gameControllerObjective: Enforce the protocol and record observations.
gameControllerMove: Admit the test, repeat the checks, preserve the evidence.
gameChallengerObjective: Find a requirement the candidate violates.
gameChallengerMove: Submit one named Go test, or report no finding.
gameCandidateGate: Original tests must pass before the challenge.
gameCounterexampleGate: A critique must become an admissible test.
gameChecks: Submitted test: two observations on the candidate
gamePassAction: Continue to final checks. No finding skips challenge checks.
gameRepairAction: One repair. Challenge test frozen. Original tests must still pass.
gameReview: You review the requirement, test expectation, and patches.
gameEvidence: Passing tests do not prove correctness.
gameOpenNote: Source and rules are available on GitHub. A license has not been chosen yet.
gameControls: Select a role to follow its move in the simulated run.
gameDiagram: Builder and challenger exchange a patch and a test through the Go controller.
launchNote: The folder selects the repository. The quoted sentence tells the agents what to change.
builderShort: Changes production code. Existing tests stay protected.
challengerShort: Proposes one test for a possible violation, in a separate session.
checkedCandidate: Original tests must pass before the challenge.
checksIntro: A submitted test runs twice on the candidate in fresh workspaces. The controller records the outcomes.
checkTableCaption: Go controller · observations on the candidate
noFindingNote: No finding skips challenge checks and continues to final checks.
boundaryIntro: The original expression matches the requirement except at equality. At exact expiry, the session must be rejected.
boundaryLocal: This expression is evaluated locally in JavaScript. It is separate from the agent simulation.
evidenceTitle: Review the patch and the test.
evidenceIntro: Inspect the source changes, the test's expectation, and the check results before applying a patch.
evidenceNote: Illustrative file previews. The local CLI creates the actual run files.
changesArtifact: Latest source patch; final checks are shown separately
reviewLimit: Passing checks do not prove correctness. You decide whether the test expectation is right and the patch should ship.
challengeExpectation: At exact expiry, Valid(100, 100) must return false.
artifactPending: Not produced at this step. Advance the run to see the preview.
artifactNoChange: The candidate leaves the boundary expression unchanged.
artifactStopped: Final checks have not passed. This source patch is unvalidated.
installContext: Build from the Tarigato source checkout:
finalSourceNote: On the final source, with any accepted test.
sessionOrder: The roles run in order, in separate sessions. Both use Codex by default.
artifactEmptyTests: Empty patch. No challenge test has been accepted at this step.
traceWorkspace: Agents work in separate copies. Tarigato saves patches for you to apply.
traceTestJoins: The accepted test joins the original suite.
traceFrozen: If a repair is allowed, this test stays fixed.
traceGateNote: Must pass before the challenger runs.
traceRepeat: Same candidate. Same test. Two runs.
traceDisclosure: Interactive illustration. The expression runs in JavaScript; the agent sessions and Go checks are simulated.
traceRoutes: When does it repair or stop?
traceExpectedFalse: Requirement: expiry at or before now is invalid.
traceTestProposal: One proposed test. Not accepted yet.
boxIntro: Give it a task in your terminal. One agent changes the code. Another tries to break it with a test. You review the patch.
miniText0: Reject the session at its exact expiry time.
miniText1: Try the boundary case the original tests missed.
miniText2: Tarigato checks the result. You decide what to apply.
miniDisclosure: Example simulation. No agents run here.
